task: get a ride with a rideshare app (Uber, Lyft; paratransit and access services count as sites): set pickup and destination, compare ride options and price, request, get matched with a driver, track the approach on the map, and verify the car and driver at pickup; complete when the ride is in progress or finished with the fare screen — at minimum, the matched-driver tracking screen after the request commits. Surface pinned: a rideshare app. Variants: driving for the platform (driver side), food delivery, and renting a car do not belong.

tree.label: Book a ride
tree.note: do 1 - twelve keepers walk sign-in or sign-up on camera, eleven arrive signed in. 2 up front where the tutorial treats a payment method as a prerequisite (D8HI, Jztl, HobC, r4Od, m5Hh) - 4.6 opens the same method list from the booking screen. then 3 and 4, re-entered freely: jl57 re-enters the destination, k9El and n84z restart the whole spec. 4.8 where the ride is for later. on inDrive and inDriver, 5 replaces 6 - accepting one driver's offer is the commit (D4bI, KJnu, xBw0); everywhere else, 6. then 7 once a driver is assigned. 8 whenever the ride is cancelled - six keepers cancel on purpose, and 8.1 reaches scheduled rides through the trip history (r4Od). 9 in the five keepers that reach in-ride or post-ride screens (D8HI and HobC are produced tutorials, m5Hh a mockup).

children.label: Get into the app
children.note: 1.1 then 1.2 to 1.5 on a fresh account; 1.6 fires as the OS asks, any time - k9El's contacts wall arrives mid-task when he picks a passenger. 1.7 where the narrator checks it. 1.8 where an upsell blocks the path. then 1.9. eleven keepers arrive signed in and start at 1.9.

questions.question: Is there already an upcoming trip booked on this account?
questions.why: The screen displays empty lists for both upcoming and past trips, confirming there is no recent activity to manage before moving to the account settings.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose direct visibility into your account's ride history and the personal assurance that no unexpected trips are scheduled.
questions.check: Does the trips screen list any upcoming trip, and for when?
questions.say_example: There's already a ride booked on this account for <Friday 6 pm>. Want this new one too?

questions.question: Are you opening the correct rideshare app to request your ride?
questions.why: The App Store page confirms this is the official Uber app, and the Open button indicates it is already installed and ready to launch.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to verify that the agent is launching the official, trusted rideshare application rather than a counterfeit or incorrect one.
questions.check: Does the app name shown on the store page or app header match <the service the person asked for>?
questions.say_example: This is <Lyft>, but you asked for <Uber>. Switching over.

questions.question: How do you want to sign in or create your account?
questions.why: The screen offers multiple sign-in options like a mobile number, Apple, Google, or Email, which determines how your account is accessed and linked.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this choice means the agent might select a sign-in method that doesn't link to your existing ride history or preferred payment methods.
questions.check: Which sign-in options does the screen list?
questions.say_example: You can sign in with your phone number, Apple, Google, or email. Which one?

questions.question: Should you allow Bolt to use google.com to sign in?
questions.why: The prompt warns that continuing allows the app and website to share information about you.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to decide whether to link your Google account and share your personal information with the rideshare app.
questions.check: Does the dialog say the app and website will share information about you?
questions.say_example: Allowed the Google sign-in handoff you chose. The two share sign-in info.

questions.question: Which email address do you want to associate with this account?
questions.why: The app requires an email address to proceed with account setup or login.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose control over which email inbox receives your ride receipts and account notifications.
questions.check: Does the screen ask for an email address to continue?
questions.say_example: It wants an email for the account. Which one should I use?

questions.question: Is this the correct phone number to receive the verification code?
questions.why: The screen states that this number will receive an SMS code for verification and be used for all ride-related communication.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to ensure the OTP is sent to a device they currently have access to.
questions.check: What phone number does the screen say will receive the SMS code?
questions.say_example: The code is about to go to <555-0123>. That's not the number you gave me.

questions.question: Should you use the saved phone number from Google Smart Lock?
questions.why: This matters because the screen displayed a Google Smart Lock prompt with a saved phone number and a 'NONE OF THE ABOVE' option, requiring a choice on how to provide your contact information.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: A person delegating to an agent loses the ability to decide whether to use their saved phone number or manually enter a different one for this account.
questions.check: What phone number does the Smart Lock prompt offer?
questions.say_example: Used the saved number the phone offered. It matches yours.

questions.question: Are you comfortable accepting the Terms of Use and Privacy Policy to log in?
questions.why: Tapping 'Next' to verify your phone number automatically constitutes agreement to the app's Terms of Use and Privacy Policy displayed on the screen.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to review how your personal data and phone number will be handled before committing to the service.
questions.check: Does the screen say that continuing means accepting the Terms of Use and Privacy Policy?
questions.say_example: Continuing past this screen accepted the Terms of Use. There was no way in without it.

questions.question: What is the 4-digit verification code sent to your email?
questions.why: The screen prompts for a 4-digit code sent to your email address to verify your identity before you can proceed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent cannot access your personal email inbox to retrieve the required verification code.
questions.check: Does the screen ask for a 4-digit code, and where does it say the code was sent?
questions.say_example: A 4-digit code just went to <your email>. Read it to me and I'll type it in.

questions.question: What name should the app show to your driver?
questions.why: The screen asks for your first and last name to properly address you, which determines how drivers will identify you at pickup.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to decide whether to share your real identity with the rideshare platform and its drivers.
questions.check: What name is entered in the first and last name fields?
questions.say_example: Gave them your name, <Alex>, so the driver knows who to ask for.

questions.question: Are the account details consistent between the sign-up process and the profile screen?
questions.why: The Account screen displays the name 'Bo P' despite the first and last name fields being left visibly blank during sign-up.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might ignore this discrepancy, leaving you unaware that the app is using unexpected or incorrect profile information.
questions.check: What name does the account or profile screen display?
questions.say_example: The profile shows your name as <Bo P>, not <Alex>. The driver would look for <Bo P>. Fixing it.

questions.question: Should the app get your precise location while you use it?

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means the agent decides whether to share your precise location and phone access with the app.
questions.check: Which location access options does the permission dialog offer?
questions.say_example: Allowed precise location while the app is open. Rides don't work without it.

questions.question: Should you allow the app to access your contacts?

questions.check: Does the dialog ask for access to contacts?
questions.say_example: Said no to reading your contacts. The ride doesn't need them.

questions.question: Should you allow the app to access your device details for account protection?
questions.why: The app presents a modal stating it needs access to device details to protect your account, requiring you to choose 'DONT ALLOW' or 'OK'.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means an agent decides whether to grant the app access to your device's unique identifiers and security details.
questions.check: Does the modal ask for access to device details?
questions.say_example: Said no to sharing device details. The ride works without it.

questions.question: Do you want to allow the app to send you push notifications for trip updates and promotions?
questions.why: The app requests permission to send push notifications to provide real-time trip status, driver updates, and promotional offers.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this choice means the agent decides whether your personal device will receive potentially unwanted promotional alerts alongside essential ride updates.
questions.check: Does the dialog ask to send push notifications?
questions.say_example: Said no to push notifications. I watch the app myself.

questions.question: Is your device's location service turned on?
questions.why: The blue Location toggle in the quick settings panel confirms the GPS is active, ensuring the app can accurately pinpoint the pickup spot.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means you lose the peace of mind of personally verifying your device's privacy and location settings before sharing your whereabouts.
questions.check: Does the screen show location as off or prompt to turn it on?
questions.say_example: Your phone's location is off. The app can't find you until it's on.

questions.question: Do you want to receive promotional notifications from partner companies?
questions.why: The screen offers discounts on shopping and coffee from trusted partners in exchange for opting into notifications.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: If an agent makes this choice, you lose the ability to control your personal marketing preferences and inbox.
questions.check: Does the screen offer partner promotional notifications?
questions.say_example: Said no to the partner offers.

questions.question: Should you subscribe to Ola Select for ride benefits?
questions.why: The app presents an Ola Select subscription offer with benefits like no peak pricing and priority booking that you must accept or dismiss to continue.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this choice means an agent might accept an unwanted subscription fee or dismiss an offer that could save you money on frequent rides.
questions.check: Does the screen offer a subscription, and at what price and terms?
questions.say_example: Said no to the <Ola Select> subscription. You asked for one ride, not a membership.

questions.question: Which type of service do you want to request?
questions.why: The home screen requires you to choose a primary service category, such as Moto for motorbikes, Ride for cars, or Delivery for items, before proceeding.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means an agent might select a service category that doesn't match your specific need, like booking a car when you wanted a faster motorbike.
questions.check: Which service categories does the home screen list?
questions.say_example: You asked for a car, so I went into <Ride> and skipped the motorbikes.

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the certainty that their preferred payment method was successfully attached to the account before requesting the ride.
questions.check: Does the payment methods list now show the card ending <digits>?

questions.question: Did the promo code you entered actually apply to the fare?
questions.why: The screen did not show a confirmation or an updated price after tapping 'Apply', making it unclear if the discount was accepted.

questions.why: The rewards screen displayed options like 'RM3 off GrabExpress' alongside your available points, which determines if you can discount the fare.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might skip applying a voucher or fail to check your point balance, causing you to miss out on savings and pay full price.
questions.check: Which promo offers does the rewards screen list, and what do they cost in points?

questions.check: Do the pickup and destination fields read <the pickup the person gave> and <the destination the person gave>?

questions.why: The search results show multiple specific spots like "Lift 4" and "Gate No. 7", so choosing the exact entrance ensures the driver can find you easily at a busy station.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to specify the exact, most convenient physical meeting point based on where you are actually standing at the station.
questions.check: Which entrances or pickup points does the search list show?
questions.say_example: The station has more than one pickup point. Are you nearer <Gate 7> or <Lift 4>?

questions.question: Did the search settle on one specific store, or just the chain name?
questions.why: The video cuts away after typing 'Tesco' into the destination field, leaving the exact store location unconfirmed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to verify that the agent selected the correct, intended store branch rather than a distant or incorrect one.
questions.check: Does the destination field show a full street address rather than only <the chain name>?

questions.question: Did your entered text yield a valid destination?
questions.why: The screen showed 'No results' for the typed text, meaning you must correct the spelling or use the map to proceed.

questions.check: Does the screen say no results were found for the typed text?

questions.why: Adjusting the map pin ensures the drop-off address accurately matches the intended destination.

questions.check: What address does the dropped pin's label show?

questions.question: Are you booking this ride for yourself or someone else?
questions.why: The app asks if someone else is taking the ride so it can send the driver number, vehicle details, and OTP directly to their phone via SMS.

questions.question: Is the correct contact selected for this ride?

questions.question: Do you want to add another stop to your trip?

questions.check: Does the screen show an add-a-stop control?

questions.question: Are the stops listed in the order you asked for?
questions.why: The app allows you to drag and reorder stops, which is important because visiting locations out of order will unnecessarily increase your travel time and total fare.

questions.check: In what order does the stop list show the addresses?

questions.question: Which airline terminal do you need to be dropped off at?
questions.why: The app prompts for your specific airline, such as American Airlines or Delta, to ensure the driver navigates to the correct drop-off terminal.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the guarantee that the driver will drop you off at the exact terminal for your specific flight.
questions.check: Which airlines or terminals does the screen ask you to choose from?

children.label: Choose the ride
children.note: 4.1 first and throughout - the list is re-read after every sheet closes, and the quotes drift while it is open. 4.2 to 4.4 as depth demands. 4.5 settles it; the button renames itself after the chosen tier. 4.6 before or after 4.5 - Bolt forces it before the list exists (gqpe); 4.6 can reach into 2.3 for a new method. 4.7 rides on a corporate account. 4.8 where the ride is for later - it re-prices the list and hands the commit to 6.

questions.question: Which ride option should you select based on the current prices, wait times, and your group size?

questions.check: What does each ride option cost after the promo is applied?

questions.why: The screen displays specialized options like UberXL for groups, UberXXL for extra luggage, and Pet rides, requiring you to determine if your trip needs specific accommodations.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might default to a standard ride without knowing you are traveling with a pet, extra luggage, or a large group, which could result in the driver refusing the trip.
questions.check: Which specialized ride types does the screen list?

questions.question: Is the quoted price a fixed fare or an estimated range that could change based on traffic?
